meta.subtitle: Revenue is up a third on the Global Blue deal and the stock trades at 7.0x forward earnings, but leverage is high and interest cover is thin

analystCommentary:
Shift4's shares have fallen to $36.31 on October 2, 2026, close to the 52-week low of $34.56 and well under half the high of $80.98. Our data does not say what drove the decline, and we have no news coverage that explains it.

The operating picture in the filing is stronger than the share price suggests. Second-quarter gross revenue rose 34%, payments volume grew 22%, and the business generated $624M of free cash flow in FY25.

The weak point is the balance sheet. Debt rose sharply to fund the Global Blue acquisition, and higher interest expense cut second-quarter net income even as revenue grew (see Financials). At this price the market is treating that leverage as the dominant risk; we think it is already more than priced in.

We rate FOUR BUY with a $40–$50 target range.

executiveSummary.companyOverview:
Shift4 Payments, Inc. provides software, payment processing, tax-free shopping (TFS) and dynamic currency conversion services. Its technology is used by restaurants, hotels, stadiums, theme parks, luxury retailers and other businesses, from small owner-operated merchants to multinational enterprises. Products include the SkyTab point-of-sale family, the Lighthouse business intelligence suite and an omnichannel payments platform.

The company added a TFS business through its acquisition of Global Blue in the third quarter of 2025. In February 2026 it collapsed its Up-C structure, converting its Founder's and Rook's shares into Class A common stock.

Shift4 was founded in 1999 and is headquartered in Center Valley, Pennsylvania. It distributes through independent software vendors, internal sales and support networks, enterprises and value-added resellers.

thesis.body: The shares trade at 7.0x NTM earnings and a 20.0% trailing FCF yield, a price that implies the business is in serious trouble. The filing instead shows strong volume growth and rising gross revenue less network fees. If Shift4 keeps generating cash and directs it to debt reduction, the equity should re-rate. The leverage is real, which is why our target sits below the Street's.

catalysts: Evidence of debt reduction from free cash flow.
Progress on Global Blue integration and synergies.
Closing of the pending account-to-account payments acquisition.
Easing of travel disruption affecting the TFS business.
risks: High leverage and thin interest coverage.
Governance transition after the Founder's departure.

financials.incomeCommentary:
FY25 revenue was $4.2B, up {+25.5%+}, after growth of 29.9% in FY24 and 28.7% in FY23. Operating margin has improved steadily, from -3.6% in FY21 to 8.4% in FY25.

Second-quarter 2026 gross revenue was $1,295 million, up 34%. Payments-based revenue rose 24% on a 22% increase in volume and recent acquisitions, and TFS revenue contributed $117 million from Global Blue. Gross revenue less network fees, the measure management uses to track the value of its merchant mix, rose 51%.

The counter-case is below the operating line. Interest expense rose to $65 million from $39 million because of debt issued for Global Blue, and interest income fell to $3 million from $19 million as cash balances declined. Net income fell to $24 million from $41 million, and the effective tax rate also rose. Growth is not yet reaching shareholders.
financials.balanceCommentary:
Total debt rose to $4.5B at the end of FY25 from $2.8B a year earlier, and net debt to $3.6B. Trailing net debt to EBITDA is 4.5x and interest coverage only 1.5x. That is the core risk in this stock: a downturn in volume would leave little margin before leverage became a constraint.

The trailing current ratio is 1.21. The 10-K also refers to outstanding Preferred Stock, which ranks ahead of the Class A common shares.
financials.cashflowCommentary:
Free cash flow was $624M in FY25, a 14.9% FCF margin, consistent with 14.8% in FY24. Capital expenditure is small, so most operating cash flow becomes free cash flow on our data's definition. The trailing FCF yield is 20.0%.

Shift4 spent -$453M on share repurchases in FY25, while its debt rose. In our view, with leverage at current levels, cash flow is better directed to debt reduction until interest coverage improves.

valuation.multiplesCommentary:
At $36.31 FOUR trades at 56.7x trailing earnings, 7.0x NTM earnings, ~5.9x FY27E earnings, 0.6x trailing sales and 7.6x trailing EV/EBITDA.

The gap between trailing and forward P/E reflects the basis. Consensus EPS of $5.21 for FY26E and $6.20 for FY27E sits far above FY25 diluted EPS of $1.08; the company reports non-GAAP EPS that excludes amortization of acquired intangibles and other items, so consensus is most likely on that basis. Even allowing for that, the forward multiple is low.

The Street is split: 12 Buy and 12 Hold, with a consensus target of $55.05, a median of $51.00 and a range of $40.00–$96.00. The low end of the Street range sits above today's price.

We have no peer multiples to compare against.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.driver: Volume growth continues, Global Blue synergies arrive and free cash flow reduces debt. The market re-rates the shares toward the Street consensus target.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.driver: Shift4 delivers close to consensus and begins reducing leverage. The forward multiple recovers part of its decline, and the shares settle above the low end of the Street target range.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.driver: Consumer spending and travel weaken, volume growth slows and leverage limits the company's flexibility. Estimates fall and the shares break below the 52-week low.

valuation.scenarioCommentary:
Base carries the most weight because it requires only partial delivery against consensus. Bull and Bear carry equal weight: the cash generation supports a recovery, while the leverage leaves the equity exposed if conditions weaken.

The result is a weighted fair value of $42.20, an expected upside of +16.2% and a bear-case downside of -25.6%. That clears our BUY threshold.

Our $40–$50 target range brackets Base and sits below the Street consensus target, reflecting the balance-sheet risk.

segments.name: Consolidated
segments.body: Shift4 reports a single segment. The MD&A breaks gross revenue into payments-based revenue, TFS revenue and subscription and other revenue: in the second quarter of 2026 these were $1,073 million, $117 million and $105 million, respectively. Payments-based revenue is the core of the business, and TFS is the new contribution from Global Blue.

moatFactors.name: Integrated software and payments
moatFactors.body: Shift4 bundles point-of-sale software, business intelligence tools and payment processing, which ties merchants into its platform. The 10-K warns that competitors include larger companies with greater financial resources, and new entrants with alternative payment systems.

moatFactors.name: Vertical focus
moatFactors.body: The company targets complex merchants in hospitality, stadiums, theme parks and luxury retail, which the MD&A describes as the experience economy. Serving those merchants requires specialized integrations that generic processors may not offer.

moatFactors.name: Distribution network
moatFactors.body: Distribution through independent software vendors, value-added resellers and internal sales gives Shift4 broad reach. Those partners are paid residual commissions, so the relationships carry a cost.

businessMoat.durability: We rate the moat NARROW. Integrated software and a vertical focus create switching costs, and steady growth in volume suggests merchants value the platform. The 10-K describes intense competition in payments and an increasing number of TFS competitors, including app-based start-ups, so the advantage requires continued investment.

points: Consensus expects FY26E revenue of ~$5.1B, up 22%, and FY27E revenue of $5.8B.
Volume grew by $11 billion in the second quarter, which supports organic growth beyond the acquisitions.

In August 2026 Shift4 agreed to acquire an account-to-account payments company for an initial payment of approximately $143 million of cash, with contingent consideration of up to $173 million. The deal adds a payment method but also more acquisition spending while leverage is high.
The forward-looking statements refer to expansion of Shift4One in 15 countries by year end, which would broaden the international business.

management.leadership: Taylor Lauber became Chief Executive Officer on June 5, 2025 and Chairman of the Board on December 17, 2025, per the proxy statement dated April 2026. Christopher N. Cruz became Chief Financial Officer effective September 1, 2025. Founder Jared Isaacman resigned as CEO in June 2025 and as Executive Chairman after being sworn in as the 15th Administrator of NASA on December 18, 2025. The leadership team is therefore new, and its record on integration and deleveraging is still being established.
management.capitalAllocation: Shift4 has been acquisitive and has also repurchased stock: Global Blue in 2025, a pending account-to-account payments acquisition in 2026, and buybacks in FY25 (see Financials). The cost has been a large rise in debt. In our view, management's next priority should be deleveraging; further acquisitions or buybacks before interest coverage improves would raise our concern.
management.governance: Per the proxy statement dated April 2026, Sam Bakhshandehpour, Seth Dallaire, Karen Roter Davis, Jonathan Halkyard and Sarah Grover are independent; Taylor Lauber and Nancy Disman are not. Shift4 ceased to be a controlled company on December 17, 2025, but may rely on exemptions from certain governance requirements until December 17, 2026, so it may not have a majority of independent directors or fully independent committees until then. For holders, that means fewer formal protections during the transition. Approximately 91% of the CEO's 2025 total target compensation was in RSUs, which ties pay to the share price.
management.insiderOwnership:
As of April 13, 2026 Jared Isaacman beneficially owned 28.66% of the Class A common stock. BlackRock, Inc. held 8.79%, Durable Capital Partners LP 8.33%, Darlington Partners Capital Management, LP 7.02% and Wasatch Advisors LP 5.30%. All executive officers and directors as a group held 1.54%.

The Founder's stake is large relative to current management's. The forward-looking statements also mention future negotiations with the Founder. In our view, any sale of his stake while he serves in government could weigh on the shares.

idiosyncratic: Leverage: the balance-sheet risk set out in Financials leaves little room if volume weakens or rates stay high.
Integration: the 10-K warns that Shift4 may be unable to integrate Global Blue or realize the anticipated synergies, and that third parties may terminate or alter contracts.

Travel disruption: the MD&A says geopolitical and global trade tensions and military conflicts have caused travel disruptions and affected consumer spending, which matters for the TFS business and hospitality merchants.
Competition: the 10-K says some competitors are larger and may offer services at lower rates, and that TFS competitors are increasing in number.
risks.systemic: Shift4 earns revenue mainly as a percentage of payment volume, so its results move with consumer spending in hospitality, entertainment and retail. A recession or a sustained travel slowdown would reduce volume and TFS revenue together. Higher interest rates raise the cost of carrying its debt.

body: BUY, target range $40–$50, based on the scenarios in Valuation.

We would add conviction on evidence of debt reduction and improving interest coverage. We would cut to HOLD if volume growth slows sharply, if consensus estimates start to fall, or if management prioritizes acquisitions over deleveraging.
